verdicts.decision_note: The client accepts the immediately preceding simple, off-the-shelf initial-build proposal and prioritizes a rapidly working prototype.
Target-specific implementation claim: the initial BOM follows the rapid-iteration sourcing approach while identifying limited custom-fabricated parts.
The custom render-style spout conflicts materially with the simple first-edition timeline, and the freelancer requests a client choice between custom and off-the-shelf paths.
The client accepts the concrete proposal to custom-fabricate stainless-steel render-style spouts, establishing an exception to the off-the-shelf V1 approach.
The client's selection resolves the preceding custom-versus-off-the-shelf uncertainty and returns the V1 approach to active execution.
The client confirms the proposed custom-fabricated raised base, adding another specific exception to the otherwise off-the-shelf V1 strategy.
The client explicitly withholds selection between functional V1 delivery and a chassis-level aesthetic overhaul pending further evidence.
The client prioritizes completion and delivery of the functional prototype, establishes a demonstration-first sequence, and places further cosmetic refinement after receipt.
The client resolves the prior scope uncertainty by choosing the functional-prototype-first path.
